hints: Set $\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=-1} = 3 - a + b = 0$ and $\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = 27 + 3a + b = 0$ to find $a = -6, b = -9$.
Integrate to get $y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + c$, substitute $(-1, 2)$ to find $c = -3$, then find $k = y(3) = -30$.
walkthrough:
Use the stationary point conditions $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ at $x = -1$ and $x = 3$ to set up simultaneous equations in $a$ and $b$:
$$3(-1)^2 + a(-1) + b = 0 \implies 3 - a + b = 0 \implies -a + b = -3$$
$$3(3^2) + a(3) + b = 0 \implies 27 + 3a + b = 0 \implies 3a + b = -27$$

Subtract the first equation from the second equation to solve for $a$ and $b$:
$$4a = -24 \implies a = -6$$
$$b = -3 + a = -3 - 6 = -9$$

Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 6x - 9$ with respect to $x$:
$$y = \int (3x^2 - 6x - 9) dx = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + c$$

Substitute the known stationary point $(-1, 2)$ to find $c$:
$$2 = (-1)^3 - 3(-1)^2 - 9(-1) + c = -1 - 3 + 9 + c = 5 + c \implies c = -3$$
$$y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x - 3$$

ai_rubric.Stationary Points and Integration: Sets up simultaneous equations from derivative (M1). Solves for $a = -6$ and $b = -9$ (A2). Integrates with constant $c$ (B1). Finds $c = -3$ (M1, A1). Obtains $k = -30$ (M1, A1).
